title: Nasma and the River That Argued
logline: Nasma fights Sabri until they discover they were always the same water.
story: Certain they were opposites and enemies, Nasma, who carried the soul's gentle breath, ran headlong against Sabri, who was journeying consciousness, wrestling with unremembered light. Each tried to push the other back uphill, and they struggled until both were spent and still. In that stillness Nasma noticed they had pooled together and could no longer tell which water had been which. What Nasma had fought so hard in Sabri was only the part of Nasma that had never been lived. Joined, they became a river wide enough to carry them both.
moral: What you fight hardest in another is most often the unlived part of yourself.
